To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequencies of single nucleotide variations and haplotypes in three drug transporter gene (ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein), SLCO1B (organic anion transporting polypeptide), and ABCC2 (multidrug resistance protein 2)) were similar between patients with antituberculosis drug induced hepatitis and patients tolerant to antituberculosis therapy.
the frequencies of single nucleotide and haplotypes in ABCB1, ABCG2 and ABCC2 are not different between ATD-induced hepatitis patients and ATD-tolerance controls.
the polymorphisms of the ABCB1, SLC01B1 and ABCE2 drug transporter genes are not associated with antituberculosis drug-induced hepatitis in the Korean population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic polymorphisms in drug transporters that are associated with the pathogenesis of antituberculosis-induced liver injury.
the relationship between the genetic polymorphisms of the drug transporter genes (SLCO1B1, ABCB1 and ABCCC2) and the risk of antituberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATDI).
the association between polymorphisms of three drug transporter genes and the occurrence of ATD-induced hepatotoxicity in Koreans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymorphisms and the haplotypes of the three transporter genes are unlikely to be risk markers for ATD-induced hepatitis.
these three drug transporter gene polymorphisms are not associated with ATD induced hepatitis in Korean patients.
the polymorphisms in ABCB1, ABCC2 and SLCO1B3 are not associated with ATD hepatitis in the Korean population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polymorphisms and/or haplotypes in drug transporter genes are not associated with drug-induced liver injury caused by the accumulation of ATDs.
the genetic polymorphism of ABCB1 (rs1045642), SLCO1B (rs4149056), and ABCC2 (rs2273697 and rs2273690) is not associated with ATD induced hepatitis in Korean patients.
polymorphisms and/or haplotypes of the ABCB1, ABCB1, and ABCC2 gene are not associated with ATD induced hepatitis in the Korean population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polymorphisms and genetic variants of these drug transporters are not associated with the development of ATD-induced liver injury.
the genetic variants of ABCB1 and SLCO1B 1 are not associated with ATD induced hepatitis.
the three drug transporter genes are not involved in the pathogenesis or susceptibility to ATD-induced hepatitis.
